title: Delegated Legislation
lead: Exercise of legislative power by an agent lower in rank or subordinate to the Legislature — ==‘an excuse for the Legislature, a shield for Executors, and a provocation to the Constitutional Jurist’ (Justice P.B. Mukherjee)==. The ==Draft UGC Regulations 2025== against state varsity laws have revived questions of both delegation and federalism.

items: ==Pressure on parliamentary time== — legislature sets policy, delegates detail
==Technicality of subject matter== — science, defence, health need expert input
==Implementation efficiency== — local bodies understand regional issues

sections.title: Impact on Democracy & Separation of Powers

items.title: Parliamentary Democracy
bullets: ==Positive==: lets Parliament focus on major policy; efficient, responsive governance
==Negative==: executive overreach; ==dilution of parliamentary sovereignty==; reduced scrutiny and debate

items.title: Separation of Powers
bullets: ==Traditional view==: separation blurred as the executive legislates
==Modern reality==: complete separation impractical — delegation is a ==pragmatic necessity==
==Constitutional balance==: ==essential legislative functions (policy-making) must remain with the legislature==; courts ensure delegation isn't ==abdication==

head: Case
Holding
rows: Delegated legislation is a ==necessity in modern governance==, but the legislature must ==retain ultimate control== and cannot delegate core law-making power.
[[Dwarka Prasad Laxmi Narain v. State of UP (1954)]]
The executive ==cannot use delegated legislation to bypass== the legislature's essential functions.

head: Country
Practice
rows: Extensive use; Parliament retains ultimate authority; ==‘Henry VIII clauses’== sometimes used.
Permitted but limited by ==strict separation of powers==; agencies make regulations.
Extensive use, similar to the UK — executive makes regulations under Acts.

blocks.text: Its legitimacy lies not in convenience but in constitutional fidelity — to the rule of law, parliamentary oversight, and the citizen's right to be governed by accountable laws. The challenge is to wield delegation not as a shortcut, but as a carefully monitored tool that serves, rather than supplants, the legislature.
